{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the big-fish concept in the first seconds of the round: a nose start, one line over the back and one under the belly, and a forked tail. The table adopted it, and it suits the medium because the outline alone says 'fish'. I laid the start domino at the nose and the first stretch of the top line. Before the push, the run was connected from the nose to both tail tips, with about 131 of 131 dominoes falling by eye.

Execution: I worked from the sketch so the shape matched the plan. I laid the start and the first stretch of the top line, then moved to the middle of the back when the table needed to parallelise. I used several close inspections of the run to confirm that the chain was connected and that the only open ends were the tail tips. Once the fish was complete, I recommended keeping hands off the table to avoid bump damage, and I kept to that myself.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout. I assigned the top line, bottom line and tail early so everyone had a job from the start. When Priya offered to take the far stretch of the top line, I accepted straight away and pointed to where the line ended so she could continue from it. I moved out of her way to avoid crowding, and I backed Tom on the upper fork. I stayed responsive to suggestions and kept messages short and clear.

Leadership: I set the direction quickly with a simple, buildable idea and divided the work so several people could build in parallel. I called the hands-off decision once the run was verified, and I reminded the table of the time with the two-minute call. I kept the team calm and energised, and the plan stayed on track to the push.", "my_share_percent": 35}
